newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh's economy grows at 5.7 pct in 1996/97.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh's economy grows at 5.7 pct in 1996/97.

text.p: Bangaldesh's economic growth picked up pace in fiscal 1196/1997 (July-June), mainly due to increased food production, the Bangladesh Economic Survey said on Thursday.

Gross Domestic Product (GDP) grew by 5.7 percent in fiscal 1996/97 (July-June) against 5.4 percent in the previous year, the survey said. The survey was released by the government as Finance Minister S.A.M.S. Kibria began announcing the country's new revenue budget for 1997/98 beginning on July 1. It said the the annual growth rate had been fixed at 7.0 percent over 1997/97-2001/2 period agai nst an average 4.5 percent during 1991-96. "The main challenge before the government has been the fight against the poverty. Higher economic growth and increased employment through raising investment are needed to eradicate poverty from the country," the survey said.
About half of Bangladesh's 120 million population live below the poverty line, according to official figures.

It estimated GDP value at $33 billion in 1996/97. "But the growth must be raised to make any significant change in the country's economic development and poverty alleviation," it said. The survey said that agriculture, which contributes 32.4 percent to the GDP, grew by 6.0 percent against 3.7 percent in 1995/96. "Favourable weather and availability of agricultural inputs including fertiliser bo osted the growth in agriculture," it said. The survey said: "The government introduced subsidy in the agriculture sector considering the economic condition of farmers and requirement of higher agruiculture production." It said food production was expected tor each a record 20.25 million tonnes in 1996/97 against 19.06 million tonnes in the previous year. But it said the growth of industrial sector faltered at 3.6 percent compared with 5.3 percent in 1995/96
